findings.title: Promise, protection, and returning benefit
findings.claim: In the focus formula, the promise joins faithful work to a benefit that protects and returns: good action is met by covering and recompense, so its result is not portrayed as lost effort.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers وعد, مغفرة, and أجر are joined to the named group who believe and perform rectifying work. Their supplied branches connect a spoken future commitment, protective covering, and a beneficial return into one relation.
findings.reader_payoff: The reward clause becomes a protected future for engaged action, with forgiveness as shelter and recompense as the return of work.
findings.containment: This preserves the plain promise of forgiveness and a great reward to believers who do good. It does not turn the verse into a commercial contract, claim that protection erases every consequence, or replace divine giving with earned control.

epistemic.reason: A citable trusted publication directly anchors all three focus occurrences and supplies a strong formula-level finding; the relation remains bounded by the focus wording.

findings.title: Reward as splinting restoration
findings.claim: Exploratorily, the focus pair behaves like dressing and splinting: damage is covered, contamination and traces are reduced, and a fractured agent is restored to load-bearing life even if healing has a history.
findings.mechanism: The focus rectifying-deeds, covering, reward, and greatness carriers contact purification at 5:6 and trace-erasure after breach at 5:13. The qualified splint branch gives the reward word a material restorative image without displacing its ordinary return sense.
findings.reader_payoff: Forgiveness and reward can be felt as a repair sequence that makes damaged life usable again, while residual history need not be denied.
findings.containment: This is an explicitly exploratory, form-distant analogy. It is not the lexical gloss of the verse or a literal bodily claim.

epistemic.reason: Focus and context Arabic anchors are supplied, but HFT roles are legacy-attributed and the splint branch is explicitly reframed and form-distant.

findings.title: Promise as a temporal horizon
findings.claim: Exploratorily, promise is a reliable temporal horizon: action can enter its appointed future, while refusal can turn the route toward it into measured delay and stationary duration.
findings.mechanism: The focus promise's appointed-time branch and annual-cycle branch contact the traced refusal, stillness, counted interval, and year sequence in 5:24 and 5:26, giving promise a temporal architecture.
findings.reader_payoff: The promise can be perceived as a horizon approached through time, with delay becoming meaningful non-entry rather than mere waiting.
findings.containment: This is an explicitly exploratory branch-proximity reading. It does not derive ordinary promise from the annual branch or make every delay a forty-year consequence.

epistemic.reason: Exact focus and context anchors are supplied, but annual and appointment readings are form-distant branch contacts carried by legacy HFT roles.
